title: burst-aware cache curator + quant-threshold translator for tenant unit-econ automation
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Tenant workloads increasingly show short-duration bursts that invalidate static prefill/cache defaults and make quantization rollouts brittle. This PR introduces a 'burst-aware cache curator' component that synthesizes tenant-specific cache/batching defaults from short-window burst profiles and a 'quant-threshold translator' that maps unit-econ signals to safe quantization tiers with automatic rollback hooks. The primary goals: 1) reduce per-token cost during steady-state while preserving tail latency during bursts; 2) enable gradual quant rollouts driven by observed econ signals with clear safety gates; 3) expose a small CLI for Ops to run dry-runs and export suggested defaults as presets-as-code.

review_comments: Marco Diaz: Overall looks good. Two concerns: (1) the default smoothing window might hide back-to-back bursts; can we add an adaptive window heuristic?; (2) need clearer safety thresholds on quant translator to prevent simultaneous rollout across all tenants.

Aisha Kapoor (author): Added adaptive_window param and implemented exponential backoff for smoothing; quant translator now requires a 3-step graded rollout and tenant opt-in flag for >Q3. See commits b4e6f78 and f1b0b7e.
Emily Chen: CI integration test flagged a race in cache warmup on cold-start; suggested addressing by moving warmup to background worker and instrumenting stall metrics.
Aisha Kapoor: moved warmup to background worker and added stall metric (telemetry/signals). Re-ran integration tests, no flakes locally.
Ravi Patel: Approving on the condition the runbook contains explicit rollback steps and SLA impact matrix (docs/ops/econ-curator.md).
Marco Diaz: Approved after small nits fixed in README and CLI help text.
